newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent holds firm as U.S. gasoline supports.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent holds firm as U.S. gasoline supports.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures continued firm after NYMEX opened stronger on the back of bullish U.S. stock data, brokers said on Wednesday.
June Brent was 15 cents up at $18.22 by 1441 GMT after trading a few cents higher after the NYMEX open.
May gas oil was 25 cents at tonne higher at $166.75.
NYMEX's June unleaded gasoline was 0.69 cents a gallon higher at 61 cents at the time, in line with its opening call.
The U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) said that gasoline stocks dipped 2.4 million barrels in the May 2 week.

The American Petroleum Institute (API) said in its weekly figures released late on Tuesday that demand for gasoline was 8.76 million barrels per day, a figure dismissed by some IPE traders as inaccurate but hailed by others as a record that gave crude a shot in the arm.
"I think that's close to a record number for gasoline, 8.76 million barrels," a broker said.
"The DEOs were not quiet as bullish as the APIs, but they still registered a 2.5 million draw down (on gasoline) and nobody was looking for it yesterday," one broker added.
"The crude looked like it was heading below $18 and the only reason I feel that we are above $18 today is the gasoline," the broker said.

EIA said that crude stocks registered a tiny rise of 100,000 barrels to 317.3 million barrels for the same period, while distillate stocks rose 2.7 million barrels for the May 2 week to 96.8 million barrels.
The APIs for distillate stocks were in line with the EIA data but for crude they showed a rise of 1.02 million barrels.

Technicaly Brent hugged the $18 area and the market needed to "convincingly break" above $18.40-50, brokers said. "It (June Brent) is still stuck in a range," one said, adding that "we need to see gasoline above 65 cents (a gallon) before we start to see crude back up at $22".
